task:
CookieJar stores a Secure cookie set over plain HTTP. A network attacker or a plaintext sibling site can then inject or overwrite a cookie that HTTPS requests will trust. This applies to plain Secure cookies and to the __Secure- and __Host- prefixes.

The cookies in scope are 'SID=12345; Secure', '__Secure-SID=12345; Secure', '__Secure-SID=12345; Secure; Domain=example.com' and '__Host-SID=12345; Secure; Path=/'. A Cookie object with secure: true counts too.

Over an untrustworthy URL, such as 'http://example.com/', setCookie must reject with an Error whose message is exactly 'Cookie is Secure but this is not a secure connection', and must store nothing. A later jar.getCookies('https://example.com/') must return [].

This holds for every prefixSecurity mode: 'silent', 'strict' and 'unsafe-disabled'. The silent mode does not hide this error. Only the ignoreError option does: with { ignoreError: true }, setCookie must resolve to undefined and must store nothing.

Trustworthy URLs keep working. For 'https://example.com/', 'wss://example.com/', 'http://localhost/', 'http://sub.localhost/', 'http://127.0.0.1/' and 'http://[::1]/', setCookie must store each of 'SID=12345; Secure', '__Secure-SID=12345; Secure' and '__Host-SID=12345; Secure; Path=/', and jar.getCookies(url) must equal [stored], with a fresh jar set to prefixSecurity 'strict' for each cookie. With allowSecureOnLocal: false, those three cookies on the local URLs in that list must reject with the same message and store nothing. With allowSecureOnLocal true, a __Secure- cookie over 'http://localhost/' is stored.

An overwrite must fail too. After 'SID=original; Secure' is set on https://example.com/, setting 'SID=attacker; Secure' on http://example.com/ with ignoreError must leave getCookieString('https://example.com/') as 'SID=original'.

The url argument may be a URL object: new URL('http://example.com/') rejects the same way, and new URL('https://example.com/') stores the cookie. setCookieSync must throw the same message, and must return undefined with ignoreError. The callback form must call back with that error and an undefined cookie.

A cookie refused this way must not reach wss://example.com/. A Secure cookie set over HTTPS must still reach it: getCookieString('wss://example.com/') gives 'SID=12345'.

The prefix checks keep their current errors. In strict mode, '__Secure-SID=12345; Domain=example.com' over http still fails with 'Cookie has __Secure prefix but Secure attribute is not set'. Non-Secure cookies over HTTP stay allowed: 'SID=12345' on http://example.com/ is stored, and getCookieString returns 'SID=12345'.

Everything else must keep working.
